# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## 1. BY PRIMARY MECHANIC

### 1.1 Loop/Path Drawing
*The solver draws a continuous line or loop through the grid.*

#### 1.1.1 Single Loop (closed)
- **Masyu** — loop constrained by black/white circle turning rules
- **Slitherlink** — loop on grid edges constrained by numeric cell clues
- **Yajilin** — loop avoiding black cells; arrow-number clues indicate black cell counts
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop through white circles with straight/turn area constraints
- **Mid-loop** — loop where black circles are midpoints of straight segments
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop alternating between moon-rooms and sun-rooms
- **Nagareru** — directional loop with wind constraints
- **Suraromu** — loop passing through numbered gates in order

#### 1.1.2 Open Paths (connecting endpoints)
- **Numberlink** — connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Pencils** — draw lines from pencil tips of specified lengths

### 1.2 Cell Shading / Painting
*The solver determines which cells are black (shaded) and which are white.*

#### 1.2.1 Shading with Connectivity Constraints
- **Nurikabe** — black cells form one connected wall; white islands match given numbers; no 2×2 black
- **Nurimisaki** — white cells connected, no 2×2 of either color; circle cells are promontories
- **Nurimeizu** — shading creates a maze from S to G; room-level shading; no 2×2 of either color
- **Kurodoko** — numbers indicate visible white cell count; black cells non-adjacent; whites connected
- **Heyawake** — room-based shading counts; whites can't span 3+ rooms in a line; blacks non-adjacent; whites connected
- **Kurotto** — circle numbers indicate sum of adjacent black groups; circles stay white
- **LITS** — place one tetromino per region; all shaded connected; no 2×2; same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent
- **Norinori** — exactly two shaded cells per region, each part of a domino
- **Nuritwin** — each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded connected; no 2×2

#### 1.2.2 Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** — black groups must be rectangles; white groups must not be rectangles; numbers indicate group size
- **Shakashaka** — place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles; numbers count adjacent triangles
- **Tilepaint** — entire tiles colored or not; diagonal-cell clues specify black counts in rows/columns

#### 1.2.3 Shading with Elimination/Uniqueness
- **Hitori** — shade duplicates so no number repeats in any row/column; blacks non-adjacent; whites connected
- **Usowan** — numbers indicate adjacent black count but one number per room is wrong; blacks non-adjacent; whites connected

#### 1.2.4 Shading with Gravity/Drop
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells in rooms (number gives count); when "dropped" they fill bottom half of grid

### 1.3 Region Division / Partitioning
*The solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.*

#### 1.3.1 Partition into Polyominoes
- **Shikaku** — divide into rectangles; each contains exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** — divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block edges
- **Sashigane** — divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends

#### 1.3.2 Partition with Number Filling
- **Fillomino** — fill numbers and partition into blocks where block size equals its number; same-size blocks non-adjacent
- **Double Choco** — partition so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape

#### 1.3.3 Partition with Chaining/Adjacency Rules
- **Chained Block** — determine black cells forming blocks; blocks must chain diagonally; unique shapes per chain

### 1.4 Number/Symbol Placement
*The solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.*

#### 1.4.1 Latin-Square Family
- **Sudoku** — place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition

#### 1.4.2 Room-Based Number Filling
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; no same number across room borders
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with 1 to N; repeated numbers in a line must be spaced apart ≥ the number's value

#### 1.4.3 Number Placement from a List
- **Nansuke** — fill blanks with digits from a given number list, crossword-style

#### 1.4.4 Orientation/Symbol Filling
- **Juosan** — fill every cell with — or |; territory clues give majority counts; run-length constraints on consecutive symbols

### 1.5 Object Placement
*The solver places specific objects (light bulbs, snakes, etc.) into the grid.*

#### 1.5.1 Light/Illumination
- **Akari** — place light bulbs; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell illuminated; no bulb-to-bulb visibility

#### 1.5.2 Creature/Entity Placement
- **Hebi** — place snakes (1–5 sequences) in white cells; snakes can't touch; line-of-sight attack rules

#### 1.5.3 Shape Placement with Evolution
- **Evolomino** — place growing polyomino blocks along arrows; each successive block adds one cell to the previous shape

### 1.6 Bridge/Edge Drawing
*The solver draws connections between nodes along grid edges.*

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect island-circles with 1–2 bridges; bridge count matches island number; all islands connected; no crossing

### 1.7 Movement/Transportation
*The solver moves given objects within the grid.*

- **Satogaeri** — move circles so each country has one; numbered circles move exactly that many cells; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; arrows can't cross; gray area sums must match

---

## 2. BY CLUE TYPE

### 2.1 Numeric Cell Clues (count of adjacent/nearby features)
Akari, Shakashaka, Kurotto, Kurodoko, Slitherlink, Usowan, Yajilin, Five Cells

### 2.2 Numeric Region Clues (count within a bounded area)
Heyawake, Nurikabe, Sto-stone, Choco Banana, Nuritwin, Norinori (implicit: 2), Tilepaint

### 2.3 Numeric Clues as Area/Size
Shikaku, Fillomino, Sashigane, Double Choco, Nurimisaki, Chained Block

### 2.4 Directional Clues (arrows)
Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Pencils, Evolomino, Yosenabe

### 2.5 Positional/Turning Clues (circles on path)
Masyu (black/white circles), Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun

### 2.6 Sequence/Order Clues
Suraromu (gate order), Hebi (snake numbering 1–5), Evolomino (growth sequence)

### 2.7 Given Numbers to Preserve/Eliminate
Hitori, Sudoku, Nansuke, Ripple Effect

### 2.8 Movement Distance Clues
Satogaeri, Yosenabe

---

## 3. BY CONSTRAINT FAMILY

### 3.1 Connectivity Required
- **White cells connected:** Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Usowan
- **Black/shaded cells connected:** Nurikabe (wall), LITS, Nuritwin
- **All islands connected (bridges):** Hashiwokakero
- **Single loop (inherently connected):** All loop puzzles

### 3.2 Non-Adjacency of Same-Color Cells
- **Black cells non-adjacent:** Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Usowan, Yajilin
- **Same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent:** LITS
- **Same-size blocks non-adjacent:** Fillomino
- **Snakes non-adjacent:** Hebi

### 3.3 No 2×2 Monochrome Square
Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, LITS, Nuritwin

### 3.4 Shape Constraints on Groups
- **Must be rectangles:** Choco Banana (black), Shakashaka (white), Shikaku
- **Must not be rectangles:** Choco Banana (white)
- **Must be L-shapes:** Sashigane
- **Must be tetrominoes:** LITS
- **Must be pentominoes:** Five Cells

### 3.5 Uniqueness in Rows/Columns
Sudoku, Hitori, Ripple Effect (with spacing)

### 3.6 Room-Based Constraints
Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Double Choco, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu, Norinori, Nuritwin, Usowan

---

## 4. BY OUTPUT FORMAT

### 4.1 Binary Cell State (black/white)
Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Heyawake, Hitori, Norinori, LITS, Choco Banana, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Chained Block

### 4.2 Loop/Path on Grid
Masyu, Slitherlink, Yajilin, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Numberlink, Pencils

### 4.3 Region Boundaries
Shikaku, Five Cells, Fillomino, Sashigane, Double Choco

### 4.4 Numbers/Symbols in Cells
Sudoku, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Juosan, Hebi

### 4.5 Object Placement
Akari (bulbs), Shakashaka (triangles), Evolomino (squares)

### 4.6 Edges Between Nodes
Hashiwokakero (bridges)

### 4.7 Movement Arrows
Satogaeri, Yosenabe

---

## 5. SUMMARY MATRIX

| Puzzle | Primary Mechanic | Output | Key Constraint Families |
|---|---|---|---|
| Akari | Object placement | Bulbs on grid | Illumination coverage, adjacency counts |
| Chained Block | Shading + partitioning | Binary cells | Diagonal chaining, unique shapes per chain |
| Choco Banana | Shading | Binary cells | Black=rectangles, white≠rectangles, size clues |
| Dotchi-Loop | Loop drawing | Loop | White circles straight-or-turn per area |
| Double Choco | Region division | Boundaries | Matching white/gray shapes per block |
| Evolomino | Object placement | Squares + arrows | Growing polyominoes along arrows |
| Five Cells | Region division | Boundaries | Pentominoes, edge-count clues |
| Fillomino | Number filling + partition | Numbers + boundaries | Block size = number, same-size non-adjacent |
| Hashiwokakero | Bridge drawing | Edges | Island degree, no crossing, full connectivity |
| Hebi | Entity placement | Numbers in cells | Snake sequences, non-adjacency, line-of-sight |
| Heyawake | Shading | Binary cells | Room counts, white span ≤2 rooms, connectivity |
| Hitori | Shading | Binary cells | Row/column uniqueness, connectivity |
| Juosan | Symbol filling | —/\| in cells | Territory majority clues, run-length limits |
| Kurodoko | Shading | Binary cells | Visibility counts, non-adjacency, connectivity |
| Kurotto | Shading | Binary cells | Circle sums of adjacent black groups |
| LITS | Shading (tetromino) | Binary cells | One tetromino/region, connected, no 2×2, shape non-adjacency |
| Masyu | Loop drawing | Loop | Black=turn+straight, white=straight+turn |
| Nagareru | Loop drawing | Directed loop | Wind direction constraints |
| Nansuke | Number placement | Digits in cells | Crossword-style from number list |
| Norinori | Shading | Binary cells | Exactly 2 per region, all in dominoes |
| Nurimeizu | Shading | Binary cells + maze | Room-level, S-to-G path, circle/triangle routing |
| Nurimisaki | Shading | Binary cells | Promontory circles, no 2×2, connectivity |
| Makaro | Number filling | Numbers in cells | Room 1-to-N, arrow=max neighbor, cross-border uniqueness |
| Mid-loop | Loop drawing | Loop | Black circles at segment midpoints |
| Moon-or-Sun | Loop drawing | Loop | Alternating moon/sun rooms |
| Numberlink | Path drawing | Open paths | Pair connection, no crossing |
| Nurikabe | Shading | Binary cells | Island sizes, connected wall, no 2×2 |
| Nuritwin | Shading | Binary cells | Two equal blocks/region, connected, no 2×2 |
| Pencils | Path drawing + partition | Paths + pencils | Pencil length, line length = number |
| Ripple Effect | Number filling | Numbers in cells | Room 1-to-N, spacing rule for duplicates |
| Sashigane | Region division | Boundaries | L-shapes, circle=bend, arrow=end |
| Satogaeri | Movement | Arrows | One circle/country, distance clues, no crossing |
| Shakashaka | Object placement | Triangles in cells | White remainders = rectangles, adjacency counts |
| Shikaku | Region division | Boundaries | Rectangles, area = number |
| Slitherlink | Loop drawing | Loop on edges | Cell numbers = surrounding edge count |
| Sto-stone | Shading | Binary cells | Room counts, gravity drop fills bottom half |
| Sudoku | Number filling | Numbers in cells | Row/column/box uniqueness |
| Suraromu | Loop drawing | Loop | Gate ordering, numbered start cell |
| Tilepaint | Shading | Binary cells (tiles) | Whole-tile coloring, diagonal clue counts |
| Usowan | Shading | Binary cells | Adjacency counts with one liar per room |
| Yajilin | Loop + shading | Loop + black cells | Arrow clues for black count, loop avoids black |
| Yosenabe | Movement | Arrows | Straight movement into gray areas, sum constraints |
